source.title: Pythia: A Suite for Analyzing Large Language Models Across Training and Scaling
source.authors: Stella Biderman; Hailey Schoelkopf; Quentin Anthony; Herbie Bradley; Kyle O'Brien; Eric Hallahan; Mohammad Aflah Khan; Shivanshu Purohit; USVSN Sai Prashanth; Edward Raff; Aviya Skowron; Lintang Sutawika; Oskar van der Wal

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates downstream benchmark accuracy across model sizes, which bears on V6, but does not fit or test held-out cross-entropy scaling laws or compute-optimal allocations.
record.gate_note: The paper does not report held-out pretraining loss curves, power-law fits, extrapolations, compute-optimal parameter/token splits, or controlled fixed-parameter architecture comparisons. Its reported benchmark scores across model sizes bear on V6. The gender-intervention LAMBADA results and term-frequency, memorization, and bias case studies do not test these scaling-law versions.
record.test_reason: The paper releases a controlled 70M–12B suite (same data, same order) and reports zero- and five-shot benchmark accuracy for every size (App. G, Tables 7–16, Fig. 8–9). That bears on whether downstream performance improves with scale (V6). The test is incidental: the authors fit no downstream law, test no prediction from loss, and report no held-out loss curves. So V1–V5 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors present Pythia as a controlled public suite for studying training dynamics and scale. They say it performs on par with OPT and BLOOM. They report case-study findings: memorization fits a Poisson process regardless of training order; term-frequency effects emerge in models ≥2.8B; pronoun-swap interventions reduce gender bias. They also find deduplication gives no clear benefit, and parallel attention does not hurt small models. They draw no conclusions about scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: Reports downstream benchmark accuracy across Pythia model sizes rather than held-out cross-entropy fits, extrapolation, or fixed-compute allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Benchmark metric and training-data condition; LAMBADA scores rise consistently with size, while WSC scores do not.

fits_no_version.finding: Term-frequency/accuracy correlation on arithmetic and TriviaQA appears only in models ≥2.8B after ~65k steps (Sec. 3.3, Table 4, Fig. 4, 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sensitivity of few-shot accuracy to pretraining term frequency emerges abruptly with model size and training steps.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202, 2023
record.problems: The downstream benchmark results are not fit to a predictive scaling relation. WSC scores are irregular, and only selected benchmark results are included here; the paper reports additional tasks and evaluation conditions.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix G reports other zero-shot benchmarks, five-shot benchmark tables, evaluations after 93k steps, benchmark plots over training, and BLOOM/OPT comparisons. These were left out to keep the extracted V6 rows focused on LAMBADA (a consistently increasing benchmark) and WSC (an irregular one).

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss reported or fitted against parameters, tokens or compute.
No fit on small runs used to predict larger runs.
All models trained on the same ~300B tokens; no compute-optimal allocation analysis.
Shape co-varies with size (Table 1); no fixed-parameter shape comparison.
Deduplicated models repeat data for ~1.5 epochs, but only benchmark scores are reported, not loss scaling.
Predictability (fitted downstream law, or prediction from pretraining loss) is not tested; only the direction of change with size is observed.
No exponents or fitting choices examined.

missing.what: LogiQA zero-shot scores flat near chance across all sizes (0.210 at 70M vs 0.224 at 12B, both suites)
PIQA, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, SciQ and WinoGrande zero-shot scores across sizes, mostly monotone gains
Five-shot WSC stuck at 0.365 for every size, and five-shot LAMBADA rising with size
Benchmark accuracy over training tokens per size (training-progress curves)

record.verdict_notes: Weak, incidental evidence. The benchmark tables were reported to show parity with other suites, not to test scaling. Model shape and learning rate vary with size, and the token count is fixed at 300B, so size effects are not isolated from hyperparameters. WSC's repeated 0.365 value suggests a constant-answer floor; WSC rows at that value are marked absent.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law form and range.
Fitting on smaller runs and predicting substantially larger runs.
Loss-minimising parameter/token allocation at fixed compute and its trend with compute.
Architecture changes at fixed parameter count.
The study reports downstream scores across model sizes but does not test prediction from pretraining loss or fit a downstream scaling/prediction law.
Sensitivity of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocation to fitting choices and setup.

relationships.condition: Zero-shot LAMBADA (OpenAI), standard and deduplicated Pythia, final checkpoints
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises at every size step from 70M to 12B in both suites (0.185→0.705; 0.192→0.710), r2–r8, r10–r16. Text also shows PIQA, ARC-Easy and SciQ rising (Tables 7–8).
relationships.display_finding: LAMBADA accuracy increased at every size step from 0.185 to 0.705 in the standard suite and 0.192 to 0.710 in the deduplicated suite, with gains also reported on PIQA, ARC-Easy, and SciQ.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Zero-shot LAMBADA (OpenAI), standard and deduplicated Pythia, final checkpoints
source_check.reason: Tables 7–8 show monotonic improvement at every size step: 0.185 to 0.705 standard and 0.192 to 0.710 deduplicated. This supports the directional component of V6 within the evaluated range.

relationships.condition: Zero-shot WSC (and, from text, LogiQA), standard and deduplicated Pythia
relationships.reason: WSC mostly sits at a 0.365 floor with erratic jumps (r17–r32), so it shows no regular improvement with size. Per the text, LogiQA stays ~0.21–0.25 from 70M to 12B (Tables 7–8). Improvement is task-dependent.
relationships.display_finding: WSC mostly remained at a 0.365 floor with erratic jumps, while LogiQA stayed around 0.21–0.25 from 70M to 12B.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Zero-shot WSC (and, from text, LogiQA), standard and deduplicated Pythia
source_check.reason: Tables 7–8 show irregular WSC gains with repeated returns to 0.365 and nonmonotonic LogiQA scores, qualifying predictable improvement by task. The stated approximate LogiQA range misses the standard 160M score: actual ranges are 0.190–0.253 standard and 0.209–0.235 deduplicated.
